Tally

Team and access

Every screen here is the live app, signed in against the seeded emulator and photographed as the person it was designed for would meet it. The design it implements is docs/team-access.md, which converged over five rounds of critique and one review by the owner.

The way in

01

A link that no longer opens anything

A spent or expired link says which it is rather than refusing in general. The live shape of this screen — the inviter’s name and what the invitation is for — needs a token that exists, which only the Team screen can mint.

Bringing somebody in

02

The Team screen

Who is already here, and who is on their way. The invite card offers two doors: a link for the volunteer whose Google account nobody knows, and an address for the one the church issued.

03

Opening the invite card

A disclosure on a phone and an ordinary card on a laptop. What is promoted on the small screen is the act, at full touch height, above eleven people — an earlier round promoted the form instead and put nobody on the first screen.

04

Naming who a link is for

Required, because a link row has no address to name it — and eight anonymous rows on a Tuesday is how a season roll goes back into a spreadsheet.

05

The link, shown once

Tally keeps only the hash, so this is the only time it can show the link. Copy, Share, or hold up a QR for the person standing beside you.

06

The QR, for the person in the room

Ten minutes, because its whole safety property is that both people are there. A photograph of it taken over somebody’s shoulder is worth nothing by lunchtime.

07

Who is on their way, and what is still to do

A link says when it stops working and offers Extend. An arrival says who spent it. A gathering the redemption could not add them to waits here until somebody resolves it — the only place that fact is ever said.

The person

08

A person, gathered in one place

Role, when they were let in and by whom, the gatherings they are on, the kiosks they paired. The 9:22 rescue is here: Team → Sam → Nursery → Add, on a phone.

The fence

09

Tonight’s gatherings, and the ones that are not yours

Locked, not hidden. A counselor at a door at 6:59 who sees an empty screen concludes the app is broken; one who sees a lock and a name knows what to do.

10

The roster, and who is on it

The chip says how many people can work this gathering. The dot beside it says somebody is asking to be added — eight pixels, no word, no target of its own, because a strip above the first row would push every name under a descending thumb.

11

Who’s on, and who is asking

The sheet leads with the ask, because it is the only thing here that is somebody’s to do. Add puts them on; Clear says it was answered — and marks it, so the person who asked can tell that from nobody having looked.

12

A gathering you are not on

Full names, whoever opened Tally today first, and an admin unconditionally — the person the list names may have been on leave since June. Under them, one button, which puts your name on the Add list and never claims to be a queue.
